newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexican leftists slain, party blames politics.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexican leftists slain, party blames politics.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist opposition party said two local leaders were shot dead on Wednesday by a member of the ruling party, and it warned of a rising tide of violence ahead of elections in July.

The Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said two of its local organisers in the town of Zaragoza, some 200 miles (320 kms) south of Monterrey in the northern state of Nuevo Leon, were shot by a bodyguard of the ruling party mayor.

"This crime has a clear link with the electoral process that is coming up, and it is part of a growing climate of hostility by the government against the opposition," the PRD said in a statement issued in Mexico City.

Both the PRD and the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in Monterrey said two brothers, Refugio and Jacobo Gallegos, were gunned down, allegedly by Manuel Hernandez, bodyguard of outgoing town mayor Cristobal Torres.

Jesus Reyhlander, a spokesman for the PRD in Nuevo Leon, accused Torres of "masterminding" the killing, which occurred in broad daylight just blocks from the town hall. The PRD said Torres' brother is the PRI candidate for mayor in July 6 elections.

PRI spokesman Cesar Velazquez acknowledged Hernandez worked for Torres, but he said the crime stemmed from a long-standing land dispute between the bodyguard and the two brothers. "It has nothing to do with politics," he said.
The PRD says hundreds of its supporters have been killed by PRI members in political violence in the last decade.

Ahead of the July 6 polls, in which Mexicans will elect a new lower house of Congress, local mayors and the governor of Mexico City, the party said the government had now launched a campaign against the opposition in the media.
"There is a deep-rooted fear that this situation, in a global manner, could lead to elections marked by violence."

The PRI has ruled Mexico at almost every level of government for 68 years, but it is expected to have a struggle maintaining its grip on power in July because of an economic crisis and other setbacks that have tarnished it in recent years.
